business_scope.primary_industry_name: Overseas Direct-Operated Hotpot Dining and Condiment Supply

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; Swiss Code of Obligations and unified federal private law with cantonal administrative implementation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 2009; in force 2010)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 1990; in force 1995)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and the People's Republic of China (signed 2013; in force for Switzerland 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), especially Articles 626a, 626b, 922 and 922a on beneficial owners and transparency; Swiss Federal Act of 10 October 1997 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 951.01); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (SR 951.02); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Transparency Act; with implementing Transparency Ordinance), as in force from 1 January 2024

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of valid passport for each shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Origin-country passport authority, then certified by a notary public and authenticated by the competent Hague Apostille authority or Swiss consular post
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (for contracting states) or Consular Legalization at the Swiss diplomatic mission for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / extract from criminal record certificate for each natural-person UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal or national criminal records authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (municipal residence certificate or recent utility bill) for each natural-person UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registry or public utility provider in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, good standing and register excerpt for any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent filing authority in the origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of the legal entity, shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized representatives against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK OFSI sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, FINMA enforcement notices, and PEP databases; additional screening for politically exposed persons, family members and close associates; verification of direct and indirect ownership at or above 25%; continuous real-time monitoring during the pre-incorporation period and before bank account opening; bearer shares are prohibited and no nominee a sham may be used to conceal ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Name Index (official public search and reservation coordination portal of the Swiss commercial registers, operated with the cantonal Handelsregisterämter)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 950 and 951 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, the registered company name must be drafted in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or, if not misleading, may contain a foreign-language element; the Latin script is required in the commercial register, so any Chinese- or non-Latin-script trade name must be transliterated consistently via official Pinyin or another accepted romanization and the registered legal name must be stated in the Swiss official language used by the canton; the name must not be deceptive, contrary to public interests, or falsely imply a public, state, charitable or regulated status.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Eidgenossenschaft / Bundes- / Fédéral / Federale / National / Nationale
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A written rejection by the cantonal Handelsregisteramt sets an objection period; the applicant or authorized representative must first file a formal objection with the same commercial registry office within 10 days of receipt, explaining conformity with the Swiss register name rules and submitting corrected translations or a revised name; if the objection is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the competent cantonal commercial-register supervisory authority or administrative court within the applicable cantonal procedural window, generally 10 to 30 days from notice; the appeal must attach the rejection decision, name-reservation receipt, proposed articles of association and legalization/translation evidence; no further name reservation is guaranteed pending the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for a full-service hotpot restaurant operator. The registered office of the Swiss AG must be a real address capable of receiving service of process and correspondence, and the physical restaurant premises must also constitute the commercial operating site under the cantonal trade and food-safety licences. A virtual reception desk or shared mail box may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address and can never satisfy the statutory registered-office or restaurant operating-licence requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85%: unannounced on-site inspection by cantonal food-safety authorities, fire-safety inspectors, labour regulators and trade-licensing police is highly probable within the first 12 months of restaurant operation; an immediate physical inspection is also possible during the licensing and pre-opening fit-out phase.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official preliminary name clearance and reservation fee at the cantonal commercial registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the articles of association (Statuten) and incorporation minutes for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss civil-law notary or cantonal notarial office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff; prevailing market benchmark for AG formation CHF 800–2,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations of foreign-language incorporation, UBO and supporting due diligence documents into German, French, Italian or Romansh as required by the registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn or court-recognized translator / certified translation service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per page or word; 15–30 pages for a standard founder-and-UBO disclosure package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization fees for passport copies, police clearances, proof of address and corporate good-standing certificates for non-Swiss shareholders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-state apostille authority or Swiss consular mission for legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention apostille fee or consular tariff; approximately USD 50–150 per document for 4–6 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and verification of UBO declarations and initial notification to the Swiss transparency register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed notary / corporate compliance provider and Federal Office of Justice transparency register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and professional benchmark; approximately CHF 150–350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal commercial register incorporation and registration fee for the Swiss AG entry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal statutory tariff; approximately CHF 300–600 plus mandatory publication costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and corporate records location for the first year, associated with the physical restaurant premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord or corporate service provider providing the registered-office annex at the operating premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a physical registered-office add-on at the licensed restaurant site, not a virtual office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC professional due diligence: PEP and sanctions screening of shareholders, UBOs and directors and preparation of the pre-incorporation compliance file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss attorney or FINMA-regulated compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed market benchmark per entity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), notably Art. 621 (minimum capital), Art. 632 (paid-up capital), Art. 643 (registration and legal personality); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV); Federal Act on the Commercial Register (HAG).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the registered-office canton (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office; publication mandated in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) with articles of association (Statuten), submitted as the application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) via the electronic eGRIS platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an AG is CHF 100,000. At least 20% of the nominal value of each share, and in all cases not less than CHF 50,000 in total, must be paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up amount is deposited in a blocked escrow account in the name of the company under incorporation with a Swiss bank, and is released only upon entry of the company in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] AG
Adopted by unanimous written consent of the board of directors on [date].
RESOLVED:
1. The subscription of the entire share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 each, is hereby ratified and acknowledged as duly subscribed and paid up in compliance with the blocked escrow deposit confirmation.
2. The registered office of the company is fixed at [address], [ZIP] Zug, Switzerland, and the relevant authority notifications are approved.
3. [Name] is appointed Delegate of the Board and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each with single signature authority, effective immediately.
4. The board members are authorised to execute all remaining formation, banking and licensing formalities, including industrial permits.
Dated: [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal public notary (Notariat) of the canton of the registered office, e.g., Notariat Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Swiss civil-law notary in the canton of the registered office to prepare the deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde), the articles of association (Statuten), and the founders' subscription declarations. All founders or their authorized proxies must appear before the notary or provide notarially certified powers of attorney. The notary verifies the company name through a pre-registration name-freedom check and certifies that the minimum capital rules are met.
required_dossiers: Founder identification documents (passport or Swiss ID)
Notarially certified power of attorney for represented founders
Draft articles of association (Statuten) in German or bilingual version
Proposed company name and purpose clauses (ISIC 5610 full-service dining)
Swiss address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies statutory defects or the proposed name conflicts with an existing registered name, submit a revised name (with three alternative names) and correct the affected clauses; the notary reissues the deed the same or next working day without restarting the formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-up minimum capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank or licensed securities dealer holding the blocked account in the name of the company under incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account with a Swiss bank, designating the company as the future owner ('AG in Gründung'). Transfer at least 20% of the nominal value of each share and in any event no less than CHF 50,000 in cash for a CHF 100,000 capital. Procure from the bank a written confirmation (Bankenbestätigung / Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) that the funds are at the company's free disposal upon registration and are blocked until then.
required_dossiers: Extract of the notarized deed of incorporation
Bank sanctions and compliance risk questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises compliance objections, provide a renewed beneficial ownership disclosure or select a second licensed bank; the bank confirmation may be substituted by a confirmation of a licensed securities dealer if the bank refuses release.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register filing and public inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton; electronic filing via eGRIS through the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) electronically to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, attaching the notarized deed, articles of association, list of directors and officers with signing powers, and the bank confirmation of paid-up capital. The application states the legal form (AG), registered office, corporate purpose (restaurant and condiment supply), share capital, and authorized representatives. The register conducts a legal review of compliance with the Code of Obligations and the name-freedom rule.
required_dossiers: Bank confirmation of blocked paid-up capital
List of the board of directors with specimen signatures
Declaration of authorized representatives and signature modalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an inquiry (Zwischenverfügung), the notary files a cure within the set deadline (usually 10 days) with corrected instruments; if rejected, an amended application is re-submitted, and an appeal to the cantonal administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) is available against a final refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entry in the Commercial Register, acquisition of legal personality and SHAB publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Handelsregisteramt enters the company in the Commercial Register and issues an official extract (Handelsregisterauszug). The AG acquires legal personality on this entry (Art. 643 para. 1 OR). The entry is published in the SHAB, and the blocked escrow capital is automatically released to the company's free operating account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed due to the SHAB processing queue, request priority handling from the Commercial Register Office; any correction to the published entry is obtained by a formal rectification application (Berichtigung) to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Steuerverwaltung), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), cantonal compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse), and Suva
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the federal UID number (automatically exchanged by the Commercial Register). Register for VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if projected annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 250,000 (restaurant food services are subject to the standard rate, and take-away deliveries to the reduced rate where applicable). Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation fund for AHV/IV/EO contributions, and enrol with Suva or a private insurer for occupational accident and non-occupational accident insurance (UVG).
required_dossiers: Turnover projection statement for VAT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority queries VAT registration, file a revised turnover projection and supporting business plan; if the compensation fund asserts a retroactive assessment, the employer registration is backdated to the Commercial Register entry date by producing the official extract and paying any due premiums.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal food safety and consumer protection authority (Kantonale Lebensmittelkontrolle) under the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (BLV), together with the cantonal commercial police (Wirtschaftspolizei) for the restaurant trade permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal restaurant operating licence (Wirtschaftsbewilligung) and food business registration (Betriebsbewilligung / Meldepflicht) under the Swiss Foodstuffs Act (Lebensmittelgesetz, LMG).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cantonal Office for the Environment (Umweltschutzamt) and the Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full EIA report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV) is required; the hotpot restaurant is below the Annex thresholds and is processed by a registration/notification procedure with the cantonal environmental office, coupled with a wastewater discharge permit from the local authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must meet the effluent standards of the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung, GSchV), including mandatory grease traps for animal fats and cooking oils; kitchen exhaust odour and VOC emissions must comply with the concentration limits of the Clean Air Ordinance (Luftreinhalte-Verordnung, LRV); food waste and used cooking oil must be collected by authorized waste operators under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA); noise from extraction and ventilation plants must respect the immission limits of the Noise Abatement Ordinance (Lärmschutz-Verordnung, LSV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Brandschutznachweis) from the cantonal fire prevention authority; structural load inspection and fit-out acceptance by the building inspectorate; occupational health and safety clearance under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and the Accident Insurance Act (UVG), including a Suva risk assessment for kitchen fire suppression systems and ventilation duct hygiene.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / AFC / AFF) — official portal: estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax administrations (e.g., Zuger Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) for income tax assessment of the Aktiengesellschaft
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG obtains its statutory Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID / IDE / IDI) upon mandatory entry in the Commercial Register (Zefix / Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt). For Swiss VAT purposes the same UID is activated at the Swiss Federal Tax Administration by filing the registration form for VAT liability (Mehrwertsteuer-Formular) via the ESTV ePortal 'EasyGov' or 'etoile' once the CHF 250,000 taxable turnover threshold is met; foreign entities with a Swiss establishment or permanent establishment must register through the same procedure by providing certified articles of association, power of attorney, and a tax domicile declaration under Art. 11, Art. 66 and Art. 67 del Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG / LTVA). The UID serves as both business identification and VAT ID, following the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None — Switzerland has no check-the-box regime. An Aktiengesellschaft is per se a tax-transparent entity for Swiss income tax purposes (subject to Swiss corporate income tax at the federal, cantonal and communal levels). No hybrid mismatch or entity classification elections are available under Swiss law; optional instruments are limited to VAT group registration (Mehrwertsteuer-Gruppierung) under Art. 15 MWSTG and group taxation for federal direct tax only under the domestic group taxation regime of Art. 75 DBG, which does not alter the legal entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 in worldwide taxable turnover per fiscal year (Art. 10 para. 1 MWSTG); no separate reduced threshold for foreign-owned entities; a lower CHF 150,000 threshold applies only to non-profit institutions and charitable organisations and CHF 100,000 for public-benefit entities — not applicable to a commercial AG operating an overseas hotpot restaurant. Voluntary registration permitted from CHF 100,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G transactions in an increasing number of cantons and at the federal level (based on eBill / Swiss QR Invoice / Factur-X and ZUGFeRD formats), while B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary. Transmission and exchange of XML and JSON-based e-invoice files is permitted and must be archived in original format for a 10-year retention period. VAT returns are filed electronically (VAT portal of ESTV 'etax'), with staggered filing dates; no instantaneous tax authority clearance or per-transaction stamping applies. Export transactions must be evidenced electronically via the customs system in force at exportation and kept in an auditable electronic export dossier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods physically transported from Switzerland to a foreign destination qualifies for the 0% VAT rate under Art. 23 MWSTG provided the exporter of record holds valid customs declarations and proof of transport. Services (including catering and condiment supply royalties) supplied to foreign recipients are zero-rated when the recipient's place of business is abroad and the service is effectively used abroad (Art. 18 and Art. 23 para. 2 MWSTG); restaurant supplies delivered inside Switzerland to foreign tourists remain taxable at the standard 8.1% or reduced 2.6% rate as applicable. The zero-rating entitlement requires that the supplier is properly registered, issues compliant invoices, and files quarterly VAT returns; input VAT on purchases attributable to zero-rated exports is fully creditable either by way of the invoice method or the net-tax-rate method where legally available.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Zollanmeldung / déclaration d'exportation) filed electronically through the Swiss Federal Customs Administration (EZV / OGD) incl. NCTS export accompanying documents and seals
Commercial invoice, purchase order and underlying export contract evidencing the sale and destination
Transport documentation: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), CMR consignment note or Swiss postal export receipt proving physical cross-border dispatch
Proof of payment: Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 confirmation or bank extract evidencing receipt of export proceeds from abroad
VAT export evidence ledger and Swiss VAT return (reporting zero-rated export turnover), maintained for the statutory 10-year retention period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Switzerland imposes no separate exchange-control repatriation deadline; however the Swiss Federal Tax Administration applies a strict substantive-evidence approach in export VAT audits and may treat missing proof of physical export or missing payment flow as an unlawful zero-rating application. Penalties under Art. 138 MWSTG include a surcharge of one to four times the tax evaded, CHF 60,000 maximum for unintentional negligence and up to CHF 180,000 plus recovery of tax for intentional violations; criminal sanctions may be imposed for wilful falsification of export records under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 186-193 StGB / Art. 118-119 MWSTG), including imprisonment of up to three years, asset forfeiture, disqualification of directors, and retrospective clawback of input VAT deductions with 4.5% compensatory interest per annum, computed from the date of the original refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale Suisse under the National Bank Act (NBA) and the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA/WZG), with prudential supervision and enforcement delegated operationally to the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full, unrestricted currency convertibility across both capital and current account transactions. There is no legislative difference in treatment between capital account contributions and current account profit remittances; dividends, branch profits, loan repayments, royalties, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred freely in CHF or any foreign currency without prior administrative approval. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to (i) Swiss anticipatory tax at 35% on dividends paid by a Swiss AG, recoverable partially under double-tax treaties; (ii) bank-internal KYC documentation proving beneficial ownership, economic substance, and source of funds; and (iii) transfer pricing documentation for cross-border intragroup payments to overseas branches or condiment suppliers. No exchange control permission from the SNB or SECO is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion quota, and no statutory repatriation timeline for export or trading proceeds. The hotpot restaurant AG may lawfully retain foreign currency receivables in Swiss or overseas bank accounts indefinitely. The only binding obligations are commercial bookkeeping under the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 957 et seq.), VAT accounting under the Swiss VAT Act, and arm's-length transfer pricing documentation for cross-border trade and intercompany settlements with the overseas branch network.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Capital Escrow Account capability and dedicated cross-border trade finance desk
Operational Account with full SIC, SWIFT gpi, SEPA, and corporate e-banking clearing matrix
Operational Account paired with Commercial Letter of Credit and import finance facilities
Operational Account for POS settlement, payroll concentration, and cash deposit automation for regional branches

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low for Stage 4 cross-border treasury. Swiss FINMA-licensed fintech providers (Yuh, Neon, and exempt payment service platforms under the Fintech Ordinance) are viable only for domestic merchant acquiring, customer wallet refunds, and small-value retail FX; they lack full banking licences and therefore cannot issue Commercial Letters of Credit, act as correspondent anchor for inbound ODI capital, or provide SIC-eligible clearing settlement for large CHF transactions. PSD2 European E-money Institutions (EMIs) holding multi-currency IBANs can legally service Swiss corporates only for payment initiation and account information services, and are structurally unsuitable for LC issuance, import financing, and UCP 600 trade documents. The recommended architecture is to use fintech rails exclusively for front-of-house collections and to route all inbound capital injections and outbound trade disbursements through Tier-1 commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or authorised signatory is generally mandatory during initial onboarding of a new Swiss corporate client with non-EU/EFTA beneficial owners. Chapter 20 of the Swiss Banking CDB and the FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance permit remote identification only where the client uses an officially recognised Swiss e-ID, holds a prior verified bank relationship, or presents notarised certified copies of identity documents from a Swiss public notary. In practice, Tier-1 banks require an in-person director interview for foreign-resident UBOs of a cash-intensive restaurant chain; a Swiss notary-certified passport copy plus a bank-to-bank KYC reference from the shareholder's home bank may substitute for physical attendance on limited operational accounts, but the signing of an LC facility agreement or cross-border loan mandate will trigger a physical two-manager interview at the principal bank branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive hotpot restaurant generating high volumes of retail CHF cash deposits without transparent terminal reconciliation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified PCI-DSS merchant acquiring agreement with POS terminal processor, daily Z-Reports and shift closure journals, cash ledger with corresponding bank deposit slips, aggregated settlement statements from the acquiring bank, electronic waiter order records, and the Swiss VAT cashbook (Kassenbuch) maintained in accordance with Swiss VAT Act Art. 78-80.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-resident director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) resident in a listed high-risk jurisdiction without a clear Swiss nexus or source-of-wealth trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies and residence permits, verified residential utility statements, short-form professional background statement, audited financial statements of the Swiss AG, tax assessment notices, share purchase agreements, and a bank-to-bank SWIFT KYC reference forwarded via the KYC-Portal or direct branch-to-branch secure channel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurrent inbound capital injections from a non-Swiss shareholder (e.g., Chinese mainland ODI) lacking a lawful purpose code or required outbound investment filing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Home-jurisdiction outbound investment approval (ODI certificate and SAFE/Foreign Exchange registration where applicable), valid Chinese business licence of the investor entity, Swiss board/shareholder resolutions authorising the contribution, executed subscription or shareholder loan agreement, fully narrative SWIFT purpose code fields, and contemporaneous capital contribution entry evidenced by the Swiss commercial register extract and statutory auditor confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intragroup advances to overseas hotpot branches for condiment supply-chain purchase settled as undocumented intercompany loans
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arm's-length intercompany agreement prepared under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and Swiss tax practice, advance pricing agreement if obtained, monthly management accounts of each overseas branch, commercial invoices with INCOTERMS 2020, house bills of lading and import customs declarations, and correspondence with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration confirming the cost contribution or margin allocation method.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer routing for inbound equity and shareholder loans: SWIFT MT103 (gpi) or MT202 for large-value injections addressed to the Tier-1 Swiss account, carrying explicit purpose codes — 'EQUI' for share capital contributions supported by notarised board resolutions and commercial register extract; 'LOAN' for shareholder loans evidenced by a signed loan agreement; 'CACA' or 'INTC' for current-account funding of overseas branch operations. For funds originating from mainland China, the remitting bank must evidence completed ODI/SAFE registration and the Swiss receiving bank must maintain full originator information and a structured payment reference matching the AG's internal ledger. Frauds and sanctions screening applies on the full payment chain; any discrepancy between the stated purpose and the AG's commercial register capital schedule triggers automatic compliance hold requiring notarised documentation. All injections are journalised against the capital contribution or intercompany loan ledger before deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement to overseas suppliers and branch vendors is executed through the Tier-1 bank's trade finance desk over four permissible rails: (i) Commercial Letters of Credit issued by the Swiss bank via SWIFT MT700/MT710 and governed by UCP 600, with presentation of transport documents (bills of lading, CMR notes, air waybills) and commercial invoice compliance; (ii) direct SWIFT MT103 corporate payments for invoices below the LC threshold, with required purpose code narrative and standard anti-money laundering screening; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) for EUR-denominated purchases from European condiment and equipment suppliers; (iv) internal branch funding in CHF via SWIFT MT101/MT103 toward the overseas branch operating accounts. All outbound channels are protected by a dual-approval four-eyes payment factory with pre-set transaction limits and a bank-facilitated FX conversion at the corporate mid-rate plus 0.25%-0.50% spread; supplier auto-pay runs execute only against matching three-way statements of purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (Vanilla) negotiated against CHF with a licensed Tier-1 Swiss bank, provided the underlying trade invoice or branch funding schedule is evidenced
FX Swap (spot/forward combination) permitted for short-term working capital and same-settlement clearing of EUR, USD, and CHF pairs
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) for converting a foreign-currency shareholder loan into CHF financing, with ISDA/CSA master agreement required

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) with net settlement for restricted-convertibility currencies (e.g., CNY, KRW) where the remitting jurisdiction limits offshore deliverability, subject to strict underlying-trade documentation

Vanilla options and zero-cost participating collars for protecting the overseas hotpot branch revenue stream from adverse FX moves, available only after credit-line approval and suitability clearance by the bank's treasury advisory desk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Shareholder Approval and Federal/Cantonal Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); Cantonal and Municipal Tax Authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting no later than six months after financial year-end; tax return generally due by 30 June following the tax year (calendar-year basis), with extensions available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and surcharge up to 30% of assessed tax; persistent failure to convene AGM or file tax returns triggers organizational deficiency proceedings under Art. 731b CO, leading to court-ordered dissolution and ex officio deletion from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Return (quarterly or semi-annual filing, or annual settlement if approved)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each VAT reporting period; for calendar-year quarters, due 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Reminder fees and statutory default interest; willful VAT evasion punishable with up to 30 days imprisonment and fine up to CHF 300,000; directors and officers may be held personally liable for withheld VAT.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Social Security Wage Declaration and Obligation Statement (AHV/IV/EO/ALV/SVV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse); Swiss Accident Insurance Fund or private accident insurer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the wage year, customarily by 31 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest and late-payment surcharges; directors can become personally liable for unpaid employer social contributions; criminal liability for misappropriation of wage deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Register Verification and Commercial Register Update Filing (if any change occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office; Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change of directors, registered office, capital or statutory provisions must be filed within 20 days; in no-change years, a formal annual audit of the shareholders' register and Commercial Register extract is performed before the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file mandatory changes within 20 days exposes directors to administrative penalties and personal liability; continued non-compliance can lead to an official notice of deficiency and ultimately court-ordered dissolution under Art. 731b CO.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit required when a company exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million; revenue CHF 40 million; average 250 full-time employees. Simplified audit applies if those thresholds are not met but the company exceeds two of three small-company thresholds (CHF 500,000 balance sheet; CHF 1 million revenue; 10 FTE), unless all shareholders validly opt out of an audit. The same audit obligation attaches to every Swiss AG unless a specific exemption law applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b) and Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is permitted for large or listed entities and mandatory for companies whose shares are listed on a Swiss or certain foreign exchanges.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not operate a central UBO filing or annual UBO re-certification as of 2025. Under Art. 697j CO and the Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance, the company and its registered corporate service provider must identify the ultimate beneficial owner upon account opening, ownership change, or change of authorised representative; an annual internal UBO confirmation before the AGM is mandatory best practice and is documented in the minutes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and Shareholders' Meetings
Share transfer records and UBO documentation file

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–3,600 per year for a registered office and corporate agent in a standard Swiss canton
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,000 for simplified audit; USD 12,000–28,000 for ordinary audit, depending on group size and account complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal Direct Tax on corporate profit: 8.5% of net (after-tax) profit, equivalent to 7.83% of pre-tax profit; combined with cantonal and communal income tax in the canton/municipality of the registered seat (e.g., approx. 4.1 percentage points in Zug Municipality), the aggregate headline rate for a fully taxable operating restaurant company is approx. 11.9% pre-tax (Zug) to 13.5% (Zurich).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for food-service companies. Since the 2020 Swiss Tax Reform (TRAF/REF), available reliefs include: (i) patent/licence box (max. 90% relief of qualifying IP-derived income), (ii) R&D super deduction (up to 150% of qualifying R&D personnel costs), (iii) 50% relief of cantonal capital tax in some cantons, and (iv) participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividend income from shareholdings >=10% or acquired for >= CHF 1 million. None of these materially apply to the active hotpot restaurant trade; the post-incentive combined effective rate therefore equals the ordinary combined CIT rate of approx. 11.9%-13.5%.
